clue.text: Unusual stamina? Yes — at the beginning giving chief support

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal state, so the word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word just before is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of yes

explanation.surface: Someone with remarkable stamina is told yes and becomes the team's chief support.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the person or thing on which everything else chiefly depends.

clue.text: Potatoes, mother's, hot initially

parts.note: MA is mother, with the possessive S kept

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: first letter of hot

explanation.surface: Mum's potatoes are served hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is the everyday name for mashed potato, so it stands for the potatoes themselves.

clue.text: I'm forward, urbane, not half talented — altogether unruffled!

indicators.note: not half means half of the word's letters are dropped, keeping just its front

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
pert means forward or cheeky
taken as written before losing half
able means skilled or talented

explanation.surface: A bold, suave, half-gifted type who is completely calm.
explanation.walkthrough: URBANE loses its last three letters; 'altogether' tells you to put everything together.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperturbable describes someone who cannot be upset, which is what unruffled means.

clue.text: Tasty feature of rugby, seemingly good, first of tries welcomed

parts.note: a scrum is a set piece in a rugby match

indicators.note: something welcomed is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pious means outwardly devout or virtuous

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of tries

explanation.surface: A rugby writer describes a tasty move in which a try is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes inside PIOUS, after PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious means delicious, so it is a stronger synonym for tasty.

clue.text: Ridiculous? Anything but, suggesting University rag day at the outset!

indicators.note: at the outset asks for the opening letter of each word in the run

parts.words: Anything but, suggesting University rag day
parts.note: first letters of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a student rag day is anything but ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag day is a British student charity event full of silly stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd and ridiculous are synonyms: both mean wildly unreasonable or laughable.

clue.text: Fail to include award, Italian

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian is left off an awards list.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is failing to include it.

clue.text: Relaxed, mellow at retro defensive building

indicators.note: something relaxed has been loosened, letting the letters that follow fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A laid-back, mellow mood at a retro venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Martello towers are small round forts built along the British coast against Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello tower is a coastal fort, a building made for defence.

clue.text: Value delightful surprise no end? Certainly

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: a treat is a delightful surprise
sure is a way of saying certainly

explanation.surface: Someone certainly values a delightful surprise that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value it highly; both are verbs.

clue.text: Excellent drink with editor on periphery

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: periphery is the edge, so only the outside letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of editor

explanation.surface: An editor enjoys an excellent drink on the edge of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning first-rate, just like excellent.

clue.text: Sudden increase concealing company's major trouble

indicators.note: concealing means holding something out of sight inside

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sudden spike in sales hides a company's serious problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering or affliction, a major source of trouble.

clue.text: Kindly media boss supporting golf tournament card

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece goes last

parts.note: the Open is a major golf championship
a heart is a playing card
ED is short for editor, the boss of a paper

explanation.surface: A kind media mogul sponsors a golf event's scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-hearted means generous and warm, which is what kindly means as an adjective.

clue.text: Referring to TV detective not so unrelenting

parts.note: re means concerning or about
Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of British television
less means not as much

explanation.surface: A remark about a TV detective who is less relentless than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorseless means pitiless and never easing up, so it matches unrelenting.

clue.text: Familiar echo? Very, what diary regularly features

parts.note: E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of diary

explanation.surface: A diarist notes a very familiar echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday means ordinary and commonplace, so familiar is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Strongrooms having five defects: not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
faults are defects

explanation.surface: Strongrooms with five flaws, apart from the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaults are secure chambers for valuables, the same thing as strongrooms.

clue.text: Wife more healthy in ship

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
haler is the comparative of hale, meaning healthy

explanation.surface: A wife feels healthier aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler is a vessel used for hunting whales, so a kind of ship.

clue.text: One very much likes fuss over ace crowd-puller, last of all

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every word in the run

parts.note: final letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A fan makes a fuss over an ace performer who draws crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: An adorer is a person who loves something greatly, i.e. one who likes it very much.

clue.text: Again transmit star race — bod excited

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; a bod is British slang for a person

explanation.surface: A spectator gets excited about a race featuring a star and wants it shown again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebroadcast is to put a programme out on air a second time.

clue.text: We hear that chap's song in Church

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: that chap is him

explanation.surface: Apparently that man's song is one sung in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the pronoun to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song sung by a congregation in church worship.

clue.text: One lowering quality of beer ads unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Beer adverts are blamed for lowering standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to reduce in worth, so a debaser is someone who degrades quality.

clue.text: Description of owl maybe cheers West New York

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
W is the abbreviation for west
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher in western New York cheers at an owl sighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny owl is a common species, so tawny is a word that describes one kind of owl.

clue.text: Guy on board survey vessel

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A man is aboard a survey ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a French man's name, and a guy is a man, so any male first name fits.

clue.text: Fancy riding or American football?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or embellish, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of preference: horse riding or American football?
explanation.definitionFit: Gridiron is the name for American football, from the pattern of lines on its field.
